units.note: οὐχ ὅλοις πεντήκοντα καὶ τρισὶν ἔτεσιν = less than 53 years: correct.

findings.quote: a supremacy that past ages cannot match and future ages will not surpass.
findings.problem: ἀνυπόστατον μὲν τοῖς ὑπάρχουσι πᾶσιν, ἀνυπέρβλητον δὲ καὶ τοῖς ἐπιγινομένοις: τοῖς ὑπάρχουσι = all those now existing (present), not past ages; ἀνυπόστατον = irresistible (cannot be withstood), not 'cannot match'. Temporal sense shifted from present to past.
findings.proposed_fix: a supremacy that no one now living can resist and that no one in future ages can surpass.

units.note: Greek at 2.8 is corrupt in the source file ('περὶ δὲ τοῦ μεντολαδιατ...'), apparently an encoding/OCR garble rather than a true lacuna; the English ('From the narrative itself it will be possible to see this more clearly') matches the standard text (περὶ μὲν τούτων διὰ τῆς γραφῆς ...). No fix proposed; the source Greek should be repaired.

140th Olympiad, Philip son of Demetrius/father of Perseus, Antiochus and Ptolemy Philopator all correct. Chapter ends mid-word (ἐξ|ίκοντο) at the seam with ch. 4; the English completes the sentence correctly from the ch. 4 opening, and ch. 4 English does not duplicate it.
Treaty figures (2,200 Euboic talents over 20 years) and Lutatius's motive (his own side worn down, τοῖς σφετέροις) correct.
